title: Energy of a block on a spring

stimulus.title: A block on a horizontal spring
stimulus.html: A block of mass M is attached to a spring of spring constant k on a level, frictionless surface. The block is pulled to x = +A and released from rest at time t = 0. It then oscillates in simple harmonic motion about x = 0. The system is the block and the spring.

drawSpec.label: Three energy bar charts, one each at x = +A, x = +A/2 and x = 0, with bars for K and U_s

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: On the bar charts, draw shaded bars to show the kinetic energy K of the block and the elastic potential energy Us of the system when the block is at x = +A, at x = +A/2 and at x = 0. Use the same scale for all three charts. A zero line is drawn for each.

rubric.point: At x = +A: K bar is zero and U_s bar has the full height; at x = 0: U_s is zero and K has the full height
At x = +A/2: the U_s bar is one quarter of the total and the K bar three quarters
The total height (K + U_s) is the same in all three charts

parts.sample: At x = +A: K = 0; U_s is 4 units. At x = +A/2: U_s is 1 unit and K is 3 units. At x = 0: U_s = 0; K is 4 units. Each chart adds to the same 4 units.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed of the block when it is at x = +A/2. Express your answer in terms of M, k, A and physical constants, as appropriate. Your equation should be consistent with your bar chart for x = +A/2.

rubric.point: Starts from conservation of mechanical energy for the block-spring system, stating the condition (no friction, so no nonconservative work)
Writes the energy at each position with the right terms: ½kA² = ½k(A/2)² + ½Mv²
accept: a term for each nonzero bar, and no K at x = +A

parts.sample: The surface is frictionless, so no nonconservative force does work, and the mechanical energy of the block-spring system is constant. At x = +A the block is at rest: E = ½kA². At x = +A/2: E = ½k(A/2)² + ½Mv². So ½kA² = ⅛kA² + ½Mv², which gives ½Mv² = ⅜kA² and v = A√(3k/(4M)) = (√3/2)A√(k/M).

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: On the axes, sketch and label graphs of the kinetic energy K, the potential energy Us and the total mechanical energy E of the system as functions of the block's position x, from x = −A to x = +A.

rubric.point: U_s is a parabola (concave up) that is zero at x = 0 and greatest at x = ±A
accept: symmetric curve, not V-shaped or straight lines

rubric.point: K is an upside-down parabola that is greatest at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A
accept: K = E − U_s at every x

rubric.point: E is a horizontal line equal to the peak of K and of U_s
accept: total flat, not sloped or curved

parts.sample: U_s: a U-shaped parabola, zero at x = 0, reaching the total at x = ±A. K: an upside-down parabola, at the total at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A. E: a flat horizontal line at the height where K peaks and where U_s ends. The K and U_s curves cross at x = ±A/√2, where each is half the total.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain how your bar charts in part (a), your equation in part (b) and your graph in part (c) are consistent with each other.

rubric.point: Links a specific feature of the bar charts to the equation: the U_s bar at +A/2 (one quarter of the total) matches the ⅛kA² term out of ½kA²
accept: the equation has one term for each nonzero bar

rubric.point: Links the graph to the bar charts: at x = +A/2 the U_s curve is at one quarter of the flat total line and K at three quarters; at x = 0 and x = +A the curves match the endpoint bars
accept: reading the graph at the three positions gives the bar heights

rubric.point: Links the constant total in all three: equal bar sums, the energy equation with the same E on both sides, and the horizontal E line
accept: all three show E constant because there is no friction

parts.sample: All three show a constant total: the bars add to the same height, the equation sets ½kA² equal at both positions, and the E line on the graph is flat. At x = +A/2 the U_s bar is a quarter of the total, which is the ⅛kA² term out of ½kA² in my equation, and it is the height of the U_s parabola at x = A/2 (U_s ∝ x²). The K bar (three quarters) is the ½Mv² = ⅜kA² term and the height of the K curve there. At x = +A and x = 0 the curves are at zero and at the total, matching the end bar charts.
